mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The current FEDFUNDS level of 1.58% is low, predicting positive returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 2.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 2.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and fall in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals an overheating economy, triggering aggressive monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2% in 3 months and UNRATE falls > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.2% in 3 months and UNRATE falls > 0.3% in 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDP growth above 2.0% and unemployment below 4.0%), the S&P 500 is vulnerable to overvaluation and profit-taking, leading to negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% and UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tight labor market, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE is below 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates strong economic activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The current INDPRO level of 109.2026 is above the 2017 base (100), indicating expansion.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO is above 100, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level (HOUST) above 1550 thousand units signals strong residential construction activity, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where HOUST is above 1550, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 260, it signals persistent inflation, which increases the risk of aggressive monetary tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL is above 260, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
